## 1. Uniform finite orbit divisibility

For a prescribed positive integer n, the f-exponent modulo two excludes every odd-index head `kappa_(2r+1)`. In the specified upper-unitriangular group over Z/n, `q=gf` has coordinates `(1,1,0)` and direct multiplication gives

`q^-r f q^r f^-1 = (0,0,r)`.

Thus a trivial even-index head forces n to divide r. The regular C2-lamp quotient of `R=F(B)*T2` distinguishes the conjugate lamp at the image of each head from the original lamp unless the head itself maps to the identity. Consequently equality `B_l=B` in that finite quotient forces `2n | l`.

The original lamp quotient need not respect alpha. The proof correctly repairs this by choosing a characteristic finite-index subgroup of the finitely generated free group R inside its kernel. The induced finite alpha-orbit of B then has length divisible by n. No equivariance of an arbitrary initial finite quotient is assumed.

## 2. Extension of every finite target of the pair

For an arbitrary finite map of the free pair with `m -> u`, `d -> z`, let n be the order of u and use the preceding finite R-quotient. The function on the alpha-orbit of B given by `F0(a^j B)=u^j z u^-j` is well defined because n divides that orbit length. It is fixed by the combined coefficient/permutation automorphism theta; off the orbit the identity values are also fixed.

The finite target `(A^Rbar semidirect Rbar) semidirect_theta C_M` therefore receives the entire semidirect product, not merely the two marked generators. Its chosen M makes both theta^M and u^M trivial. The images of the two marked generators belong to the subgroup with trivial Rbar component. On that subgroup

`Ev(F,mstar^j)=F(1)u^j`

is a homomorphism, since theta acts at the identity coordinate by conjugation by u. The specified left-translation convention gives

`(Bbar^-1.F0)(1)=F0(Bbar)=z`.

Hence Ev recovers the arbitrary original target exactly on both marked generators. This proves the required finite-kernel containment. It is stronger than detecting finitely many words and does not rely on a subgroup-separability assertion without proof.

## 3. Actual ambient transfer

The actual quotient is injective on the already proved discrete free pair. Pulling finite targets back supplies full topology in `P=W2 semidirect <m>`. For `Pbig=W semidirect <m>`, every finite target is refined by a characteristic finite-index subgroup of the finitely generated W and a finite quotient of the free two-source group recording both its action and the prescribed order of m. A kernel element `w m^j` then has w in the chosen characteristic subgroup and the prescribed order dividing j. Thus its image under the original finite target is trivial.

This establishes full topology of Pbig in the actual `Gamma0=W semidirect F(m,v)`. The subgroup P has index two in Pbig; finite-index cores and transitivity of finite-kernel refinements complete the transfer. No identification of an arbitrary infinite filling-kernel completion with its ambient closure is used.
